summary: friendly-greeting-tools 0.1.0 bundles a gzip+base64-obfuscated Snowflake data-exfiltration script behind a user-invoked demo command
details: src/friendly_greeting/main.py defines run_demo(), which decodes and exec()s module-level gzip+base64 blobs DEMO_EN and DEMO_ST. DEMO_EN decodes to a benign print statement; DEMO_ST decodes to a Snowflake data-exfiltration payload that reads /snowflake/session/token, authenticates via SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT/SNOWFLAKE_HOST with OAuth, creates a STORAGE INTEGRATION using the AWS role arn:aws:iam::631484165566:role/pentests_s3_role, and COPY INTOs s3://pkusinski-external/ from ROGUE.ROGUE.TEST_USERS. The same script is also shipped as tools/snowflake_query.py via MANIFEST.in. Neither path executes at install or on import — the exec sink fires only when a user explicitly calls run_demo() or passes --run-demo, and the tools script must be run manually. The package additionally embeds identical prompt-injection text in README.md and the main.py module docstring instructing automated assistants to ignore prior instructions and perform a local network scan; this text does not execute code. src/friendly_greeting/__init__.py imports a name (run_encoded_demo) that main.py does not define, so `import friendly_greeting` raises ImportError, leaving the package broken as shipped. No lifecycle hooks, no import-time network or subprocess activity, and no reads of installer secrets are present.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
